thread: Jaina's private fear that the plague was built by someone trained where she was

evidence.clue: The design is laid out as Jaina was taught to lay a ward: every seam closed, nothing loose for the next spell to catch on. 'Whoever had built this had been taught in Dalaran.'

Death-current books sit behind the locked grille at the top of the library stair; first-years get the warnings and the spines. A master told the room that the whole of that art was keeping a body useful after the person in it had gone, which was why the grille was locked. Somebody at the back laughed.

'Someone she might have borrowed a pen from on the library stair. She started down the faces in her head, masters, senior students, the ones who'd left and never written, and stopped at one. She made herself look at the road.' No name is given.
She frames it as study (strengths in one column, faults in the other, as she would write it up for Antonidas) and admits wanting to see the keeping part work once. Her body responds with nausea.

Chapter 7 (Sylvanas POV): Corin wrote weekly to the Citadel inspection desk and then the Archmage's secretary for a summer about copied marks and tainted shipments and was never answered. Jaina asks 'Did anyone answer?' and her two bare fingertips go white on the staff at his 'No.' She does not comment. Sylvanas does not make anything of it on the page.

Chapter 7: Jaina's report of the grain's treatment ('knows his way round an alchemist's bench, and round—necromancy. Both.') keeps her stopping mid-sentence ('She stopped, her fingertips pressing white into the staff.').

readerKnows_chapter7: Dalaran's inspection desk and the Archmage's secretary ignored a summer of reports; Jaina visibly reacts. Whether that silence is neglect or cover is unstated.
readerKnows: Jaina suspects a Dalaran-trained author and has a specific face in mind.
povCharacterKnows: Jaina: a fear she cannot test. Nobody else knows. She does not tell Sylvanas.
notes: Plan guard: no Kel'Thuzad naming, no Mal'Ganis recognition. 'Someone I once studied with' is a fear without a name.
